subclass_note: ESCALATED prerequisite: a proved local finite-type theorem ensuring vectorwise finite quasi-R action on arbitrary based integrable modules (without finite weight multiplicities), together with finite supported transfer-correction closure at that generality. Reviewed all seven steps and independently read Bao-Wang 1403.0039v2, Sections 2.1-2.3 (Lemmas 2.2-2.3, Propositions 2.4/2.6, Theorems 2.7/2.9, conditional associativity and Remarks 2.10/2.14), and Lusztig printed pp.192-194/PDF201-203 and based Definition 27.1.2 on printed214/PDF223. The finite-type coefficient test itself is compatible with the source and local global/extremal argument. The affine Gram determinant is 1-q^4, giving a nonintegral coefficient; the p=[2] extension map is valid modulo p because E_1g=pF_0v, F_0^(r)g=0 for r>=2 and F_1g=pF_1^(2)F_0v, with higher raising degrees zero. Its graph lattice has unchanged A0 crystal chart because 1/p is in qA0, and the coefficient -(1-q^2)/(1+q^2) is not Laurent integral. However step 2.1 closes case (c) by asserting arbitrary finite-type based pairs have finite-dimensional weight components. The direct sum of infinitely many trivial based modules satisfies the stated four axioms and integrability but has infinite zero-weight dimension, refuting that premise. Step 2.2 also does not establish finite supported correction closure for such infinite-multiplicity inputs merely by citing finite weight intervals. A root-vector/Weyl-operator local-finiteness argument would require additional proved quantum prerequisites absent from this carrier. Bao-Wang imposes vectorwise finite action and its Remark 2.10 retains finite-weight O_int conditions; Lusztig 27.1.2 assumes finite-dimensional modules. The current owner direction explicitly preserves arbitrary based pairs in finite Cartan type, so I have neither narrowed that claim nor represented an incomplete replacement as repaired. Required owner decision: supply/authorize a complete local finite-type arbitrary-based action-finiteness and supported-correction prerequisite, or explicitly disposition the intended broader contract.
